headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a tuple of strings (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.content:
Here’s a quick guide to help you pick a short‑running film (≤ 2 hrs) that’s still within walking distance of Times Square in New York City:

| Theater (walking distance) | Typical walk time | How to find showtimes & runtimes |
|-----------------------------|-------------------|----------------------------------|
| **AMC Empire 25** (Broadway & 7th Ave) | ~5 min | Visit the AMC website or app; the “Showtimes” tab lists each film’s runtime next to the title. |
| **Regal Cinemas Times Square** (Broadway & 7th Ave) | ~5 min | Check Regal’s site or the “Now Showing” section; runtimes are shown in the film description. |
| **AMC Lincoln Square 13** (Broadway & 34th St) | ~10 min | AMC’s “Showtimes” page lists runtime; you can also use the “Movie Details” link for each film. |
| **AMC 8th Avenue** (Broadway & 8th Ave) | ~10 min | Same as above – runtime appears in the film details. |
| **Regal Union Square** (Union Sq & 14th St) | ~15 min | Showtimes page lists runtime; click the film title for full details. |

### How to filter for ≤ 2‑hour films

1. **Open the theater’s showtimes page** (most sites list runtime right next to the film title).  
2. **Look for the runtime column** (e.g., “Runtime: 1h 45m”).  
3. **Filter manually**: skip any film listed as “2h 05m” or longer.  
4. **Optional**: use the theater’s “Search” or “Filter” feature (if available) to set a maximum runtime.

### Sample movies that usually run ≤ 2 hrs (check current showtimes)

| Film | Runtime | Notes |
|------|---------|-------|
| *The Grand Budapest Hotel* | 1h 47m | Comedy‑drama, often in 3D. |
| *Moonlight* | 1h 51m | Drama, often in 2D. |
| *Lady Bird* | 1h 44m | Coming‑of‑age comedy‑drama. |
| *The Social Network* | 2h 0m | Exactly 2 hrs; still qualifies. |
| *Arrival* | 1h 56m | Sci‑fi thriller. |
| *The Imitation Game* | 1h 59m | Historical drama. |
| *The Shape of Water* | 1h 58m | Fantasy‑drama. |
| *The Big Short* | 1h 58m | Comedy‑drama. |
| *The Farewell* | 1h 48m | Comedy‑drama. |
| *The Hunt* | 1h 57m | Thriller. |

> **Tip:** Many theaters now offer a “Short Films” or “Under 2 hrs” filter on their showtime pages. If you’re in a hurry, look for that option.

### Quick steps to book

1. **Choose a theater** from the table above.  
2. **Navigate to the showtimes page** (usually a link labeled “Showtimes” or “Now Showing”).  
3. **Select a film** that lists a runtime ≤ 2 hrs.  
4. **Pick a showtime** that fits your schedule.  
5. **Reserve tickets** online or at the box office.  

Enjoy your movie night—just a short stroll from Times Square!
